hints.content:
We expand the parentheses using the **distributive property**:

$\blueD A(B+C)=\blueD A\cdot B+\blueD A\cdot C$

We can also think about the problem using an area model:

[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: Two rectangles of different sizes make up a larger rectangle. At the left, a rectangle has the width of nine x squared and a length of two x squared. At the rectangle on the right, it has a width of negative sixteen with a length of two x squared.

hints.content:
Here's how the solution goes, algebraically:

$\begin{align}
&\phantom{=}\goldE{2x^2}(9x^2-16)
\\\\
&=\goldE{2x^2}(9x^2)+\goldE{2x^2}(-16)
\\\\
&=18x^4-32x^2
\end{align}$

Here's how the solution looks in terms of the area model:

[[☃ image 1]]

Inside of this rectangle is eighteen x to the fourth. At the rectangle on the right, it has a width of negative sixteen with a length of two x squared. Inside of this rectangle is negative thirty two x squared.
